chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Safwan, from 'Isim ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from Ali (peace be upon him), that he used to say:
"The thaniyyah (two-year-old) from camels, the thaniyyah from cows, the thaniyyah from goats, and the jadha'ah (one-year-old) from sheep."

key_terms.الْثَّنِيَّةُ: A two-year-old animal, specifically referring to the age category for camels, cattle, and goats in ritual contexts.
key_terms.الْجَذَعَةُ: A one-year-old sheep, the required age category for sheep in ritual sacrifice.

ai.seo_question: What are the required ages for camels, cows, goats, and sheep in Islamic ritual sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq from Imam Ali, establishes the precise age criteria for sacrificial animals, defining 'thaniyyah' as the second year for camels, cattle, and goats, and 'jadha'ah' as the first year for sheep. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is critical for validating both the ritual sacrifice (udhiyah) and the tithe (khums), ensuring the animal has reached physical maturity without being overly aged. The specification reflects the detailed legal methodology (usul al-fiqh) of the Ahl al-Bayt in refining general Quranic commands into actionable fiqh rulings.
